feeds.title: UK Crime Stats Blog
feeds.description: UK Crime Stats, the leading public resource for maps, analysis and reporting of monthly crime data in England and Wales, growing by 500,000 crimes a month.

feeds.title: Kingsley Napley Blog » Criminal Law
feeds.description: Get information about criminal law from Kingsley Napley LLP.

feeds.title: Russell Webster Blog
feeds.description: Russell Webster drugs, crime & social media expert. Blogs on probation, payment by results, Transforming Rehabilitation, digital engagement.

feeds.title: Crime Files Blog
feeds.description: Crime Files is a reading community bringing together avid crime and thriller fans from three publishers: Hodder & Stoughton, Headline Publishing Group and Quercus Books.

feeds.title: Promoting Crime Fiction
feeds.description: From an early age I have been a lover of crime fiction. Discovering like minded people at my first crime conference at St Hilda's Oxford in 1997, I was delighted when asked to join a new group for the promotion of female crime writers. In 1998 I took over the running of the group, which I did for the next thirteen years.

feeds.title: Crime Book Junkie
feeds.description: In Crime Book Junkie, Noelle shares her thoughts and reviews on Crime fiction, psychological thrillers, action thrillers, horror, murder mysteries, and further Book-writing adventures. Author Noelle Holten is an award-winning blogger at www.crimebookjunkie.co.uk.

feeds.title: Crimes Through Time Blog
feeds.description: Join me as I explore real crimes through time. From murder to robbery, the brutal to the strange, the heartbreaking to the amusing. I will be digging into historic cases, prominent figures, changes in law, investigative techniques, crime scene analysis, forensic developments and more.

feeds.title: The Venetian Vase
feeds.description: The Venetian Vase started as a supporting site for two books: 100 American Crime Writers and 100 British Crime Writers. The blog is edited and maintained primarily by Steven and Chris Routledge. Read Book reviews, Interviews, and funny little strolls down the Crime Fiction lane.

feeds.title: Crime In Mind Blog
feeds.description: We want to support discoveries about what helps people with mental disorder who have been victims of criminal behaviour, or perpetrators of criminal behaviour, and their families, and the clinicians and others who treat them and, indeed, the wider community when its members are in contact with these problems. Explore the research, comments, debates and more in our blog.

feeds.title: The BSC Blog
feeds.description: All about current issues on crime, criminology and criminal justice. This blog is run by the BSC office. The British Society of Criminology aims to further the interests and knowledge of both academic and professional people who are engaged in any aspect of work or teaching, research or public education about crime, criminal behavior and the criminal justice systems in the United Kingdom. The Society has been in existence for 60 years and has a wide-ranging membership based here and overseas.

feeds.title: Damppebbles
feeds.description: Crime fiction blog featuring reviews, author guest posts and other fabulous booky things (with the odd psychological thriller and horror novel making an appearance!) Hello. My name is Emma and damppebbles is my baby. I'm in my early forties and live in South Oxfordshire with my husband and two young children.

feeds.title: Crime and Justice Studies
feeds.description: A digest of news from the Centre for Crime and Justice Studies and beyond. We create lively spaces for collaboration and learning, where conventional criminal justice policy agendas are scrutinized and challenged, fresh knowledge and ideas are discussed, and transformational solutions are developed.

feeds.title: A Crime Readers Blog
feeds.description: This blog started as a challenge to read as many books as I could by authors who were appearing at the Harrogate Crime Writers Festival. Once that was over I realised that I enjoyed writing this blog nearly as much as the actual reading, so have kept it going.

feeds.title: The Turnaround Blog » Crime Fiction
feeds.description: Turnaround has been distributing books in the UK and overseas since 1984, and as you can imagine, everyone who works here is a veritable book-nut. The Turnaround Blog is our place to share all this with you. Whether you're a bookseller, reviewer or a general book lover, stick around for regular book content on both brand-new releases and hidden gems. Keep up to date with the latest in crime genre, authors, popular books and more!

feeds.title: Raven Crime Reads
feeds.description: Have a good wander across Raven Crime Reads for reviews and crime news. The blog author with nom de plume is Raven spends all their free time reading and reviewing books across a range of genres preferably crime for many major publishers and online sites.

feeds.title: The Crime Lab Blog
feeds.description: We specialize in bringing true crime experience to our valued customers. Our flagship is Virtually Killed-A Crime Scene Investigation. Explore exciting videos, white papers and blogs about a whole host of topics. From psychopaths to forensics.

feeds.title: National Criminal Justice Arts Alliance (NCJAA) Blog
feeds.description: Our blog aims to present opinion-based pieces from our network. We want to hear what our community is doing in prisons or community settings - whether it is an art intervention, research or perhaps a question or problem they have been facing or a good practice example they would like to highlight, we post it all here. Our aim is to ensure the arts are used within the criminal justice system as a springboard for positive change. We represent a network of over 900 individuals and organizations that deliver creative interventions to support people in prison, on probation and in the community.

feeds.title: Criminology Tales
feeds.description: The blogs are bite-sized and hopefully accessible reads for anyone interested in crime, harm and criminology. Current categories include COVID Criminology; Crime Issues and Theory; Crime Media Art and Representation; and Guest Blogs and Interviews. My name is Dr. Natasha Mulvihill and I am a senior lecturer in Criminology and researcher at the Centre for Gender and Violence Research at the University of Bristol, in the UK.

feeds.title: Crime Time
feeds.description: Explore imaginative book reviews, features, and news about the best crime fiction in the UK and around the world. Crime Time is your leading source for all the updates on crime fiction in the UK.

feeds.title: Crime Traveller
feeds.description: Exploring true crime, criminal behaviour and the criminal mind and brain through research and psychology. Delve into true crime cases, justice and punishment and the research and theory behind criminal behaviour and the criminal brain.

feeds.title: National Crime Agency
feeds.description: The National Crime Agency aim is to protect the public from the most serious threats by disrupting and bringing to justice those serious and organised criminals who present the highest risk to the UK.

feeds.title: The Crime Writers' Association
feeds.description: For all lovers of crime fiction and non-fiction. Books, events, and news from authors of the Crime Writers' Association. The Crime Readers' Association offers a unique perspective on the largest community of crime writers in the world: the Crime Writers' Association.

feeds.title: Crimestoppers Blog
feeds.description: Crimestoppers is an independent nationwide charity that gives you the power to speak up to stop crime, 100% anonymously. Learn more about crimes, criminal activities, tips and advice to stay safe, people's stories and more!
